claims.head: The Hurricanes should tilt the ice
claims.body: The Hurricanes have been the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Islanders around the middle. Expect the Hurricanes to spend more of the night in the Islanders’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

notes.text: Taylor Hall is out (upper body injury) and has missed the last 8 games. Nikolaj Ehlers has taken his spot beside Logan Stankoven and Jackson Blake. That line has had 83% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 66:02 together, up from 60% with Hall.
Jordan Staal is out 1-2 months (calf tear) and has missed the last 10 games. Mark Jankowski has taken his spot beside Jordan Martinook and Nikolaj Ehlers.

Alexander Nikishin is out (not injury related) and has missed the last 8 games. Juuso Välimäki has taken his spot beside Shayne Gostisbehere. That pair has had 77% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 69:28 together.
Logan Stankoven has started killing penalties: on the ice for 26% of the team’s shorthanded time in 16 games, up from 1% last season.
Mathew Barzal is on the injured non-roster list (knee injury) and has not played this season. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Matias Maccelli is on injured reserve and has missed the last 6 games.
Ryan Pulock is out 2-4 weeks (upper body injury) and missed their last game. Matthew Schaefer has taken his spot beside Adam Pelech.
Mitchell Chaffee was added to the roster on Oct 20 and has played beside Casey Cizikas and Kyle MacLean.
Kyle Palmieri is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 14 games, down from 37% last season.

stakes: The Islanders go in tied for third in the Metropolitan with 16 points, 10 points behind the Hurricanes, first in the NHL.

NYI.head: A steep climb for the Islanders
NYI.body: Even though the Islanders have home-ice advantage, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, the Islanders will be without Barzal. To pull this off, the Islanders can start with getting good looks, plus Ilya Sorokin stealing the show.

CAR.head: The Hurricanes should be in control
CAR.body: Even though the Islanders have home-ice advantage, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, the Islanders will be without Barzal. It’s on the Islanders to make it a game, and they can if they get good looks.

story.head: The Hurricanes are on a heater
paras: The Islanders (7-5-2) lost 4-0 to Edmonton on Saturday. The Hurricanes have won four straight, the last a 7-0 rout of Winnipeg. Going in, the Hurricanes are first in the NHL and the Isles fourth in the Metropolitan (tied for 17th in the NHL).
The Hurricanes’ record (.812) is about what their chances are worth. The Islanders’ record (.571) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.515), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Hurricanes take away shots from the point (lowest) and create more chances on the penalty kill than anyone (1st), but give up a lot of dangerous shots (32nd). Carolina has scored 3.94 goals a game, the third most in the league, and allowed 2.19, the second fewest. As for the Islanders, they get their defensemen shooting (1st), have had some of the league’s best goaltending (2nd) and spread the ice time through the lineup (3rd). The Hurricanes’ power play (7th) could do real damage against the Islanders’ penalty kill (29th), though their penalty killers create chances of their own going the other way.

Sebastian Aho (9 G / 12 A / 21 P in 16 GP) leads the Hurricanes in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games and seven goals in ten games against the Islanders since 2023-24. Logan Stankoven (10 G / 5 A / 15 P in 16 GP) has a team-high ten goals, tied for sixth in the NHL. Bo Horvat (7 G / 7 A / 14 P in 14 GP) is tied for the Islanders’ scoring lead. Matthew Schaefer (4 G / 10 A / 14 P in 14 GP) shares it.
Pyotr Kochetkov (10-0-0 / .929 SV% in 10 GS) has been terrific for Carolina and will likely start. Ilya Sorokin (6-4-0 / .911 SV% in 10 GS) has been terrific for the Islanders and will likely start.
The Hurricanes usually control more of the chances than the Islanders do.

items.text: Pyotr Kochetkov has won all ten of his starts this season, already the longest winning run to open a season by any goalie in franchise history.
The Hurricanes have been without Taylor Hall, Jordan Staal and Alexander Nikishin for several games.

The Islanders are newly without Ryan Pulock, have been without Matias Maccelli since Oct 17, and have had to make do without Mathew Barzal all season. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, no team is missing more right now.
Mark Jankowski has seven goals on chances worth about 3.0 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
